headline: 5 Rules For Holding Opposing Protests In The Same New York City Parking Lot
body:
1. All competing banners must be printed on eco-friendly, biodegradable fabric to ensure that when they inevitably get tangled, the cleanup crew doesn't have to deal with microplastics.
2. Protesters are required to share a singular, neutral-branded power strip for their megaphones, with a strict 'alternating decibel' schedule to prevent acoustic interference.
3. Every heated argument must be paused for sixty seconds every half-hour to allow a local hot dog vendor to pass through the middle of the crowd to maintain his daily revenue quota.
4. Opposing chants must be vetted by a volunteer jazz drummer to ensure they are synchronized into a cohesive, if somewhat chaotic, rhythmic structure that doesn't annoy the local residents.
5. Any accidental eye contact between members of the opposing camps must be immediately followed by a polite, formal nod of acknowledgment regarding the high cost of Manhattan commercial real estate.
caption: New York City: Where even the most intense political ideological clashes eventually have to figure out how to share a curb. #NYC #ProtestLife #Politics #Satire (satire)

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 5 provides the most concrete and vivid imagery—specifically the 'hot dog vendor' needing to cross the protest lines to hit his quota—which grounds the absurd premise in a relatable, slightly affectionate NYC reality. It successfully avoids the 'AI slop' tendency by using specific, rhythmically varied details rather than just rehashing a list of tropes.
